question.problem: Given that $f(x) = \dfrac 1 {x^3}$ and that $F'(x) = f(x)$, calculate $F(x).$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that integration is the opposite of differentiation. So, if $F'(x) = f(x),$ then integrating both sides of this equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}^{′}(x) & =f(x) \\ \int {F}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ F(x) & =\int f(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $\dfrac 1 {x^3}= x^{-3}.$ So, we can use the power rule with $n=-3$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x) & =\int f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {x}^{-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{-3+1}}{-3+1}+C \\  & =-\frac{{x}^{-2}}{2}+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}+C.\end{aligned}
$$
